learning_objectives: L1: Identify core list operations: .append(), .pop(), .sort(), sorted(), enumerate(), zip().
L1: Define dictionary and set operations: .get(), .items(), set(), intersection, difference.
L2: Explain how the with-open context manager guarantees a file is closed.
L2: Compare .sort() (in place) with sorted() (returns a new list).
L3: Write a list comprehension that filters values by a condition.
L3: Build a frequency-counter dictionary from a block of text.
L3: Read a text file line by line and write a summarised report to a new file.

mini_lessons.title: Working with Strings and Text Processing

concepts.title: Cleaning and Reshaping Text
concepts.explanation: Strings are immutable Unicode. Slice with text[start:end] where end is exclusive. Clean with .strip() to trim whitespace and .lower() to normalise case. Substitute with .replace('old','new'). Break a string into a list with .split(',') and rejoin with ', '.join(items). Format output with f-strings: f'Cleaned: {value}'.
concepts.worked_example: raw='  Ada, Grace , Alan '; parts=[p.strip() for p in raw.strip().lower().split(',')]; ', '.join(parts) -> 'ada, grace, alan'

concepts.title: Organising and Filtering Lists
concepts.explanation: Add items with .append() and remove by index with .pop(). Sort in place with .sort(), or get a new ordered list with sorted() while leaving the original untouched. Filter with a comprehension: [x for x in data if condition]. Track positions with enumerate(items) and process parallel lists together with zip(a, b).
concepts.worked_example: scores=[72,-3,90,55,-1]; sorted([s for s in scores if s>=60]) -> [72, 90]

mini_lessons.title: Structured Data with Dictionaries and Sets

concepts.title: Key-Value and Unique Collections
concepts.explanation: Dictionaries store key-value pairs. Read safely with .get(key, default) to avoid a KeyError, and iterate with for key, value in d.items(). Sets hold only unique values: set(my_list) strips duplicates instantly, a & b gives the intersection, and a - b gives the difference.
concepts.worked_example: freq={}; [freq.__setitem__(w, freq.get(w,0)+1) for w in 'the cat the mat'.split()]; freq -> {'the':2,'cat':1,'mat':1}

mini_lessons.title: File Input/Output and Simple Data Streams

concepts.title: Reading and Writing Files Safely
concepts.explanation: Open files with a context manager: with open('data.txt','r') as f, and the file closes automatically even if an error occurs. Iterate line by line (for line in f) to handle large files without loading them into memory. Parse each record with line.strip().split(','). Write results with open(path,'w') and out.write(text + '\n').
concepts.worked_example: with open('log.txt') as f: rows=[ln.strip().split(',') for ln in f]  # each row -> [user, action]
